config.title: Berlin Parking Zones - FAQ
config.subtitle: What the zones charge, when they stop, and whether the resident permit is worth it.

items.q: How many parking zones does Berlin have?
items.a: There are 103 managed parking zones in Berlin, spread across 8 of the 12 districts. Mitte has 30, Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf 24, Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg 17, Tempelhof-Schöneberg 15, Pankow 6, Spandau and Neukölln 4 each and Steglitz-Zehlendorf 3. Lichtenberg, Marzahn-Hellersdorf, Reinickendorf and Treptow-Köpenick have no managed zone at all. The districts run their own zones, which is why the hours and tariffs are not uniform across the city.

items.q: How much does street parking cost in Berlin?
items.a: Hourly tariffs are 2, 3 or 4 euros. Thirty-eight zones charge 2 euros, forty-six charge 3 euros, sixteen charge 4 euros, and three Pankow zones sit between 2 and 3 depending on the street. The expensive end includes the Ostkreuz-Kiez and Arena Süd zones in Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg, the Neukölln zones along Karl-Marx-Straße, and zone 29 in Mitte.

items.q: Which Berlin parking zones charge on a Sunday?
items.a: Only one. Zone 29 in Mitte, which covers Karl-Liebknecht-Straße, Alexanderstraße, Mollstraße, Torstraße and Rosenthaler Straße, runs Monday to Sunday from 09:00 to midnight at 4 euros an hour. That is 105 charged hours a week, the most in Berlin. Every other zone is free all day on Sunday.

items.q: What time do Berlin parking meters stop charging?
items.a: It depends entirely on the zone. Ten zones run until midnight, 37 stop at 22:00, 49 stop at 20:00 and seven stop at 19:00 or earlier, including four Spandau zones that stop at 17:00 on weekdays. Nothing charges before 09:00 anywhere in the city. At 20:00 on a Saturday, 37 of the 103 zones are still charging and 66 are already free.

items.q: How much is a resident parking permit in Berlin and how long does it take?
items.a: The Bewohnerparkausweis costs 20.40 euros and is valid for up to two years. You can apply if your registered main address is inside the zone, and you need a copy of the fully unfolded front of your vehicle registration document, Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil 1. Processing takes up to four weeks, longer if the application is incomplete, so the online application is the faster route. Renewal can be requested a month before it expires.

items.q: Does a Berlin resident parking permit guarantee me a space?
items.a: No. The official wording is explicit: the permit lets you park free of charge inside your approved zone during the charged hours, but it gives you no claim to a parking space. It also only works in your own zone. Park in the neighbouring zone and you need a normal ticket.

items.q: How do I pay for parking in a Berlin zone?
items.a: Either at the machine, which usually takes coins only, with the ticket placed face up behind the windscreen, or through an app. Berlin works with the smartparking platform and six apps currently plug into it: EasyPark, Yellowbrick Flowbird, moBiLET, PayByPhone, Parkster and PARCO. The apps bill by the minute and need no paper ticket. If a machine is broken, call the service number printed on it, then use another machine or pay by phone.

items.q: Is there a maximum parking time in Berlin zones?
items.a: Generally no. You may stay as long as your ticket is valid. There are signed local exceptions, such as the four-hour cap around Gendarmenmarkt in zone 1, and fees or hours can differ on short stretches inside a zone, so the sign at the kerb always overrides any list.

items.q: What is the fine for parking without a ticket in Berlin?
items.a: The ladder is federal, so it is the same in every district: 20 euros for up to 30 minutes, 25 euros up to an hour, 30 euros up to two hours, 35 euros up to three hours and 40 euros beyond that. Enforcement is the part people underestimate. Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg alone puts 50 parking wardens on the street in two shifts, Monday to Saturday from 09:00 until midnight, and inside a zone they also note vehicles missing the green environmental sticker.

items.q: Which new Berlin parking zones are starting?
items.a: Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg is converting the district in stages. Friedenstraße started on 1 April 2026, Alexandrinenviertel on 1 June, and Mehringplatz plus the Graefekiez extension on 1 August. Askanischer Platz, zone 58, starts on 1 October 2026 at 4 euros an hour until 22:00, and Samariterviertel, zone 31, starts on 1 December 2026 at 3 euros an hour until midnight. Blücherstraße, Rathaus Yorckstraße, Richard-Sorge-Viertel, Hausburgviertel and Alt-Stralau follow in 2027 and 2028.
